Attachments for ghost messages are currently saved to disk like regular ones, but they should stay in memory instead. I need to reorder the logic so the ghost status is determined before attachments are saved—right now `saveAttachments` happens at line 828 while the ghost determination comes later at 848. The ghost flag only depends on `command.ghost`, `ws`, and `threadId`, so I can compute it earlier.

Then I'll modify `saveAttachments` to accept a ghost flag and either write to disk or store in a `Map` on the session called `ghostFiles`. The attachment serving route will need to check this map first before hitting the disk. There's also a complication: the renderer posts attachments via `/attachments` before sending the chat message with `/ghost`, so files might already be on disk by the time I know they're for a ghost message.

I should also make sure that when ghosts are dropped, their files get cleaned up from memory. And I want to verify whether the renderer is using the WebSocket `attachments` field or the HTTP POST route — checking the renderer composer will clarify the upload path.
